overview: A one-page Department of State list of papers, dated October 15, 1945, indexing three earlier items concerning Taiwan (Formosa): a March 9, 1932 report from Taipei on personnel changes in the Taiwan Government-General and accompanying biographies; a report from Chongqing on Chinese publicity concerning an incompletely described “formal operation”; and a memorandum by Stanley K. Hornbeck containing a historical sketch of Taiwan and commentary on Japanese colonial administration and Taiwanese attitudes. The sheet also records cross-filing references within the State Department’s decimal file system.

subfiles.title: Department of State list of papers concerning the government of Taiwan
subfiles.about: An index sheet identifies three earlier reports or memoranda concerning government, administration, publicity, and public attitudes in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists a March 9, 1932 report numbered 11 from Taipei, attributed to Ketcham, on personnel changes in the Taiwan Government-General, with biographies enclosed and a notation that it was cross-filed under 894.00. It also lists a March 9 report numbered 342 from China at Chongqing, attributed to Tours, concerning Chinese publicity about a “formal operation,” although the description is truncated. A third entry records a July 29 Far Eastern Affairs memorandum by Hornbeck: its first section is primarily a historical sketch, while its second discusses Japanese administrative practices in Taiwan and the character and attitudes of the Taiwanese people; it is cross-referenced to 894.014/2.

interest: This sheet is useful chiefly as a provenance and filing guide: it reveals the range of materials once associated with the subject file and points to related decimal-file locations. Its references connect prewar reporting on Japanese colonial personnel and governance with wartime Chinese interest in Taiwan and a broader State Department assessment of the island’s history, administration, and population. The truncated entry and apparent OCR errors also illustrate the difficulties of reconstructing dispersed archival files from administrative indexes.
